title: Consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic on the frequency of psychiatrically associated reporting events in emergency medical services: a monocentric, exploratory, retrospective cohort study.
summary: The purpose of this study is to objectify the subjective perception that the amount of emergencies with a psychiatric background has increased since the beginning of the Corona pandemic at the 3 emergency physician work sites of the Section of Emergency Medicine at Ulm University Hospital, Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine. The Covid 19 pandemic led to restrictions in all aspects of public life. Among other things, this also affected outpatient and inpatient care structures for psychiatrically ill patients. Furthermore, it has become obvious that the restrictions in daily life can lead to psychological problems in quite a few people. Subjectively, this has led to an increase in the number of emergency medical calls with a psychiatric indication. This has been confirmed in an initial database query. However, it cannot be excluded that this could be a purely statistical effect. To objectify the hypothesis above, the number of emergency doctor visits with psychiatric reporting prior to the pandemic (January 2015 to February 2020) will be compared with the number of visits during the pandemic (March to November 2021). Furthermore, if there is a correlation, the effects of the restrictions, such as the introduction of the mask mandatory, on the numbers of emergency doctor visits with psychiatric indication will be analyzed. This is a retrospective analysis of existing data. As a secondary question, problems relevant to the emergency medical care of psychiatric patients under pandemic conditions are to be identified and recommendations for future pandemic events are to be extrapolated from this.
conditions: psychiatric disorders - in the case of emergency medical visits, only a syndromal classification of the disease pattern is possible.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all emergency physician visits with psychiatric indications during the study and comparison period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All emergency medical visits with psychiatric indications are analyzed, and thus each patient assigned to the particular visit.
Exclusion criteria:
none
